## Reaction rates by mass action (`reactions`) {#sec-ch06-mass-action}

### Summary

The kinetics module turns a list of reactions into one rate per reaction. Each rate is a rate constant times the
product of the reactant concentrations raised to their stoichiometric coefficients. The species tendency is the
stoichiometric matrix times the vector of rates. Every other scheme of this chapter supplies either a rate constant
or a replacement for the mass-action product.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Reaction rates $r_j = k_j \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}}$, @eq-ch06-mass-action-rate.

**Data.** Temperature [K], pressure [Pa], molar concentrations [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] in, rates [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] out.

**Placement.** `Kinetics.forward`, called by the driver once per step.

**Activation.** The `reactions` block of the YAML file; always on when it is present.

**Guarantee / limits.** Pointwise and exact for the given rate constants; concentrations floored at $10^{-300}$.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $c_i$, molar concentration of species $i$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$]; $k_j$, rate constant of reaction
$j$ (units set by the reaction order); $\nu_{ij} \ge 0$, forward order of species $i$ in reaction $j$ [-];
$S_{ij}$, net stoichiometric coefficient of species $i$ in reaction $j$ [-] (products positive, reactants
negative); $r_j$, rate of reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$].

The scheme is always on. Reversible reactions are split into a forward and a reverse column; the reverse rate
constant is the forward one divided by the equilibrium constant from the NASA-9 data of @sec-ch02.

### Derivation

For an elementary reaction $j$ the law of mass action gives

$$
r_j = k_j(T, p) \prod_i c_i^{\nu_{ij}} .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-rate}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-rate is computed in `forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}). Summed over reactions, the
species tendency is

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d} c_i}{\mathrm{d} t} = \sum_j S_{ij}\, r_j .
$$ {#eq-ch06-mass-action-tendency}

@eq-ch06-mass-action-tendency is formed by the caller, for example as `stoich @ rate`, with $S$ the `stoich` buffer
built in `reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}}). Both are exact given $k_j$; the only
modification is the concentration floor described under Numerical method.

For a reversible reaction the reverse rate is $k_j K_{c,j}^{-1} \prod_i c_i^{\nu'_{ij}}$, with $\nu'_{ij}$ the
product coefficients and $K_{c,j}$ the concentration equilibrium constant. The derivation of $K_{c,j}$ from the
Gibbs energies is not drafted yet.

### Numerical method

The rate constants of all reaction forms are evaluated first, one evaluator module per form, in the fixed order
Arrhenius, coagulation, evaporation, three-body, Lindemann, Troe, SRI, KB fall-off. Each evaluator runs under
autograd on a copy of the concentrations, so its derivative $\partial k_j / \partial c_i$ comes back with the rate
constant (and $\partial k_j / \partial T$ when `evolve_temperature` is set). Concentrations are floored at
$10^{-300}$ ($10^{-30}$ in single precision) before the power, so that $0^0$ and $r_j / c_i$ stay finite. Evaporation
columns replace the product by the condensate concentration alone (@sec-ch06-evaporation). A finite entry of the
optional input `kf_override` replaces the computed rate constant and zeroes its concentration derivative.

The figure of the evaluator order is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| options | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.hpp KineticsOptionsImpl >}} | `KineticsOptionsImpl` | `reactions` |
| YAML reader | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp KineticsOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}} | `from_yaml` | `reactions` |
| stoichiometry, evaluators | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}} | `reset` | always |
| rates | {{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}} | `forward_with_rate_constants` | always |
| Python binding | {{< code python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp bind_kinetics >}} | `bind_kinetics` | always |

: Code map of mass-action rates. {#tbl-ch06-mass-action-code}

1. `from_yaml` reads `reference-state` (`Tref`, `Pref`) and then each reaction family from `reactions`; reactants
   and products are sorted into vapor and cloud species, vapors first.
2. `reset` builds `stoich` (species by reaction, reversible reactions appended as negated columns), registers one
   evaluator per family, and builds `forward_orders`, in which an evaporation column has order one in its
   condensate and zero in its gases.
3. `forward_with_rate_constants` returns the rates, $\partial k / \partial c$, the optional $\partial k / \partial
   T$, and the raw rate constants; `forward` returns the first three.

### Limits

Untested hypothesis: for reversible reactions the temperature derivative of the reverse rate constant is the forward
one copied ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}), without the
temperature derivative of $K_{c,j}^{-1}$. It matters only with `evolve_temperature` on and reversible reactions; no
test covers that combination.
